note: Settings > Change log. One entry for every five site versions (66-70, 71-75, ...), newest first.

items: Stats: a button for the team picked in the logo bar, a Starters filter that counts only points from starts, and a Starts column.
Rosters and Stats: the @ or vs and the NFL logo sit centered under the Wk header.
Scoreboard: your team's game (Settings) leads the list with a ring in your team's color and a My Matchup label.

Scoreboard: labels over each game, highest first: Championship Preview, Game of the Week, My Matchup, Playoff Preview, Playoff Stakes, Revenge Game, the 1.01 Bowl or Draft Stakes, and Division Rivalry.
Scoreboard: a win-chance bar from MFL's projections with each side's percentage and players left (5/6) under it; tighter cards fit all six games on a phone.
Rosters: a Trend column with arrows for who's heating up or cooling off. Low-volume players are skipped, and players who are out get an OUT mark instead of an arrow.
Rosters: a Heat column and the Heat Check up top in the player box; role archetype icons on each row; a Player Card tab with the icons on the front and what they mean on the back.
Award chips stack beside the player's name, and Player of the Week shows its week (POTW:4).
Injury tags come from MFL's injury report first, with ESPN as the fallback.
Section menus in the top tabs: Game Day, League Now, Rookie Draft and Reference have a ▾ that opens their pages, replacing the button rows on those pages. A one-time note explains the move.
Scoreboard: a tighter header (status beside the title, week strip and Compact / Expand on one row) and a gold shimmering border on the Game of the Week.
Standings on a phone held upright open on logo, record, GB, Pct, Div and PF; swipe right for team names. Seed chips sit on the team logos everywhere.
Ticket Helper on iPad: player names stay on one line.
Ticker: Game Day sections with live FBP scores (with or without each side's top two players), top scorers with hot and cold marks, NFL scores and the weekend's games still to come.
Trading Floor > History: How it played out follows every asset forward through later trades until a player is released or not kept, with what the other team got in each later deal.

Ticker settings: pick and reorder its sections (trade deadline, MFL Power, Heat Check, hot and cold players, playoff odds, matchups, last week's scores, trade block, latest moves, Press Box). Run one line or two, each with its own speed, direction and spot: under the tabs or pinned to the bottom of the screen. It starts as one line at the bottom.
League Now > Rosters: new L3 column, each player's average over his last three games (bye week skipped).
The front page leads with the newest Press Box article and its photo, with the next two as compact links. The Press Box headlines can also run on the ticker.
Scoreboard: players whose NFL team is off this week now say Bye instead of Final.
Tighter page headers: the as-of line sits beside the page title and the page buttons move up under it.
Beta > Navigation Lab: try three ways the page buttons could move up into the top header.
Trading Floor: “How it played out” now counts playoff points from real playoff games (not consolation games), and trade cards fit phone screens.

FBP Journey timelines: every stop in a player's FBP career, with team logos, how he arrived (A auction, D draft, T trade, W waivers) and how he left. Vertical on phones, side-by-side lanes on wider screens, with a Show details switch. On the Player Page, in Reference > Players (Player Journey, up to three players at once) and in each Trading Floor trade.
2019 and 2020 waiver claims, free-agent pickups and trades are now on record, so journeys and the trade history go back to 2019.
The footer and League Now header show when the data was last refreshed and whether it was an automatic or a commissioner refresh.

New ticker under the tabs: MFL Power Rating with each team's change since last week and a season sparkline, then Heat Check (team Heat Scores, the 12 hottest and 12 coldest players). Swipe it either way, tap anything to open that page, or hide it in Settings.
Injury chips are back for players on long-term IR, PUP or suspension (Achane, Tracy and others) that ESPN's weekly injury report leaves out.

New Beta tab after Settings, for trying out unfinished features. First up: Player Cards, a trading card for every player built on the prototype player ratings, with a foil by tier (holo 90+, gold 80s, silver 70s, bronze), a stat back you flip to, and tilt on mouse or phone.
Cards come in a stack: swipe the top card away to see the next one, Back brings them back one at a time, tap to flip. A Grid view shows them all at once.

Action photos come from Wikimedia Commons with credit on the back; players without a usable free photo keep their headshot. The search now skips other people who share a player's name (Cam Ward the hockey goalie, Michael Thomas the safety).
Phone tilt works however you're holding the phone, and the iPhone tilt button sits at the top of the page.
Player search on League Now > Rosters looks across all 12 rosters and jumps to the Player Page. On Stats, the search filters the table and shows every match, past the Top limit.
NFL trade deadline: Kirk Cousins (MIN), Keenan Allen (SF) and Josh Downs (KC) show their new teams. A traded player's old games no longer show as byes.
Devin Cho's Superflex column: who's ready for the two-QB league and who isn't. Devin and Rex Callahan now have photos on their bylines.
Rex Callahan's rumor mill on a taxi-squad exemption for rookie QBs, plus an update on the seventh playoff spot.
New Press Box tab collects every column, newest first and grouped by week, with a filter for each writer. Standings links to it under the latest three, and every column links back to it.
Settings has a Default team. Rosters, Stats, Projection accuracy, the Mock Draft and Reference > Franchises open on that team; Reference itself still opens on Home.
Tap a team on League Now > Standings to open its roster.
Projection accuracy on League Now > Analytics filters by FBP team (pick as many as you like) and by position. The chart and both tables follow the filters.
Players in an FBP IR slot no longer get a second IR chip on the roster page; they keep only their NFL injury chip. The Player Page shows one IR chip at most.
The installed app, taskbar and browser tab use the FBP shield on a transparent background. Phone home screens keep the square icon.
On Rosters, the week's projection and the two opponent columns are centered under their headers, with the opponent logos lined up.

New: League Now > Hospital (beta). Every injured player on an FBP roster, sorted into wards by expected stay (Triage, Observation, Ward, Long-term care, Season-ending), with a census of each team's injured points and salary. Tap a patient to see his injury, expected return week, recent production, the latest report and a short guide to that kind of injury.

1st Team and 2nd Team All-FBP players get a gold or silver background and ring behind their photo everywhere it shows: the Scoreboard, Players, Rosters, the Player Page, Awards and the Hospital. The Hall of Fame's All-Time team is diamond, with a diamond trim across the top of each card.
Press box columns can lead with a photo, caption and credit, and shared links to a column show that photo. Sal's Week 9 recap is the first.
Team logo pickers on Rosters, Stats and the Hospital sit in one row on desktop and two rows of six on phones, like Reference > Franchises.
Once a week is in the books, the Scoreboard moves on to the next week right away, with each team's lineup, projected points and the matchups, instead of waiting for MFL to turn the page.
State of the Team's Up next line shows the coming week's opponent, and its win chance and playoff swing update with every refresh.
On phones, the League Now section buttons sit in two rows of four.
The Scoreboard's defense chip reads ON D.
Scoreboard Compact view: tap Compact for a whole matchup on one phone screen: each starter's photo, name, points and projection, with the 1st/2nd Team chip, ball and RZ beside the photo.
Inactive players get a red IN chip and a grey photo with a DNP stamp.
Rosters shows each player's current NFL injury designation (Q, D, O, IR…), and the team picker shows all twelve logos in two rows of six, like Stats.
Records boards sit in a tidy three-across grid, and the All players / Free agents / Rostered / Starters bar fits phones cleanly.

New Stats page on League Now: every player's FBP points by week, with filters for how many, position, week range and All players / Free agents / Rostered, sortable columns, a Heat column, award chips, and Heat Check tints on each week.
Tap a team logo on Stats to highlight its players. On phones the table opens on the player, points and average, and its header row stays pinned as you scroll.
Menu buttons across the site are now one connected bar with square corners, so more fits on a phone; the League Now menu shows Analytics again on desktop.
Pull down from the top of any page on your phone to reload it.

Heat Check in Analytics: how often each team's starters and every player went Nuclear, Hot, Cold, Bust or into Witness Protection, with a Heat Score; chips for those weeks show on game logs and schedules.
Projection accuracy in Analytics: who lands closest to his MFL projections and who misses most.
Rosters shows each player's NFL opponent this week and next. Game Day's menu now runs Scoreboard, Players, NFL Scores, Ticket Helper.
The Player Page shows the latest news report, with older ones folded underneath.
Scoreboard: NFL game scores in each player's matchup line, a red tint for players in the red zone, and a grey tint once a player's game is over (fading toward the middle for starters).
Players no longer jump between WR and FLEX as scores change.
Game Day Players shows live estimated points for free agents, taxi and IR players until MFL posts official numbers.

New FBP Power Score on League Now > Power Rankings (beta): strength now, keepers, auction cash and draft picks, with keep/drop suggestions for next season that anyone can flip to see the effect. 2027 values are priced for SuperFlex, and rookies get a value floor from their NFL draft slot. MFL's rating stays below for comparison.
New Player Page: tap Player Page in a player's box on Rosters for his bio, news, game log, schedule, contract, FBP career, awards, NFL career stats and journey.
NFL Scores: tap a game to open its line score, top FBP scorers, scoring plays, leaders and team stats.

Scoreboard: NFL logos, each player's matchup (vs or @) with the weather, a football and RZ chip when his team has the ball, Defending for defenses, and press-and-hold to drag matchups into your own order. Stat lines use the space in the middle on phones.
Players filters (all, free agents, rostered, starters), every meeting in Matchups, prospect boxes with photos and school logos on the Big Board, and a Points Back column on FBP Home.
Big games stay Hot after the final whistle.
Rosters: State of the Team, a weekly write-up for each team with last week's result, team news and what's up next. It folds closed.
Rosters: season points, points per game and position rank count every player's full season, taxi and free-agent weeks included.
Player boxes get profile labels (scoring styles like Mr. Reliable, and roles like Volume King) and a Journey tab with every FBP move he's made.
Defenses show their NFL logo, owners show as first name and last initial, and the team-logo row keeps its place when you pick a team.
The game log lists FBP points right after the result, and NFL logos show in the game log and schedule.

New League Now > Rosters, right after Standings: tap a team logo for its roster grouped by position, with bye weeks, FantasyPros rest-of-season ranks, this week's projections, season points and rank, award chips, and this year's salary plus future salaries with the escalators.
Tap any player for his box: the latest RotoWire news, his game log with FBP points each week, his NFL schedule, his FBP analytics and a salary breakdown.
Each team gets a Face of the Franchise and a points-by-week chart against the league average, with its toughest loss, luckiest win and record in above-average weeks.
The logo row scrolls away and the section tabs stay pinned at the top.
Swiping between sections works on iPhones.

New League Now > Analytics: points left on the bench, luck vs. expected wins, beating MFL's projections, playoff odds week by week, and a cost analysis of starting lineups (what each team starts in salary, where the money goes by position, and whether the pricier lineup wins).
Analytics tables sort by any column, charts flip order, sections fold up with a Collapse all button, and team logos stay pinned on the left when a table slides sideways.
Game Day > Players adds free agents, taxi squad and IR players, a Rostered players only checkbox, S/B/T tags for starter, bench and taxi, and leaves out players who were inactive.
Swipe left or right on a phone to move between the main sections.
Team records and playoff records stay on one line on Reference > Players.
Scoreboard names stay on one line, shrinking to fit, with chips wrapping beneath.

Player photos on the Scoreboard light up by how a player is doing: a nuclear blaze for monster games, flames for players running hot against their projection, and cold, bust and blank looks for the ones letting their team down.
New Game Day > Players page: the week's top scorers at every position, with photos, FBP team logos, Show more, and free agents marked FA (with a checkbox to hide them).
Projections now go back to week 1, so past weeks show hot, cold and bust players too.
MFL's projected points on the Scoreboard: each player's projection before kickoff, and a projected total under each team's score that updates live during games.
A Projected This Week row on each Matchups game, from the lineups as currently set.
Scoreboard cleanup on phones: seed chips sit on the logo corner, scores of any length fit beside the who's-winning bar, and the record line stays on one line.
Defenses show what they've earned their points with (points allowed, sacks, interceptions, fumble recoveries, TDs) and go by nickname, like Jaguars D.
Names and stat lines wrap cleanly on phones.
The 🥶 only goes to the lowest-scoring team that has actually had a player take the field.
Scoreboard chips for this season's award holders: 1st Team and 2nd Team All-FBP, MVP, RoY, ToY, Player of the Week and more, plus team chips like Top Manager, Luckiest and Unluckiest.
A who's-winning bar under VS on every Scoreboard game, tipping toward the team in the lead.
Notes on the Awards page and the Scoreboard that awards are leaders so far, not final until the regular season ends.
Scores line up in every Scoreboard game, and taxi squad and IR rows are tinted yellow and red.
This change log, in Settings, and Settings sections that fold open and closed.
The mock draft board holds still as picks fill in, then moves up one pick at a time to keep the pick on the clock centered.
New NFL Scoreboard on Game Day: every week of the NFL season with scores, kickoff times, TV networks and byes, refreshing every 30 seconds while games are on.
Game times everywhere show your own time zone (PST, EST and so on).
New Reference > Players tab: every player's record when he's in an FBP starting lineup, back to 2019, plus every FBP team he's started for.
Reference > Records > Season PPG shows every team-season, this one included, with records and headers you can tap to sort.
League data now refreshes every morning after waivers, not just once a week, and a week only counts as played once its NFL games are final.
Rex Callahan's rumor-mill column on a seven-team playoff.
Menu reordered: Game Day, League Now, Awards, Rookie Draft, Reference, Off-Season, By-Laws, Settings.
New Game Day tab, home of the Scoreboard and the new Sunday Ticket Helper: the best three games to put on multiview for each FBP matchup, window by window, with NFL RedZone as the fourth screen.
Scoreboard details: player photos, injury tags, playoff seeds, each team's record and last-three average, 🔥/🥶 for the week's high and low scores, and every team's bench, taxi squad and IR.
Scoreboard week picker to look back at any week's lineups and results, and lineups that fit on phones.
Shared links now preview as the page you shared (Playoff Picture, Draft Order, a column's headline) instead of plain Footballpalooza.
Standings add PB: how far each team is behind the league's top scorer.
Sal's Week 8 recap column.
Mock draft team hauls moved beside the draft board on desktop.
New live Scoreboard: every FBP game with lineups, live points and player stats.
Trade of the Year shows the top five trades as headlines you can open.
A pick used in the same season's draft now counts as the player taken with it, and a player's points stop counting toward a trade once he leaves the team.
Trade of the Year leaves out commissioner pick bookkeeping.
Smaller press box headlines on League Now, newest column first.
The header always shows the site version.
Share button in the header: opens your phone's share sheet for the page you're on.
Record-pace tags on the 1st Team All-FBP, with the best season ever at each position, and they wrap neatly on phones.
All-FBP player photos sit on their FBP team's colors.
Trade of the Year shows what traded picks turned into and how each deal has played out since.
